---
title: "14 · Energy-Based Models"
code-tools: false
toc: false
---

An image becomes a vector of signs, and a network with one spin per pixel stores images as the valleys of an energy landscape. In the Hopfield network the Hebbian couplings place a valley at every stored pattern, single-spin updates only lower the energy, and the network completes damaged or partial images. The other stored patterns act as noise, which limits the capacity to about 0.138 N random patterns, and the Hebbian rule also leaves false memories such as inverted patterns and mixtures. Temperature turns the energy into the Gibbs distribution, and the Boltzmann machine learns its couplings from data by maximum likelihood, so that each coupling changes by a data correlation minus a model correlation. Hidden units let pair couplings describe correlations among many visible units. In the restricted Boltzmann machine each layer is sampled in one step, contrastive divergence shortens the sampling, and the trained machine generates new digits and new Ising configurations.
